about: Settings for firmware.py. Each option picks the PlatformIO base environment ('env'), adds -D flags ('flags'), can force other options ('forces'), and names the output file ('slug'); 'env_rules' pick an environment for a combination. Format: README.md.

options.label: Wi-Fi
options.help: Wi-Fi, MQTT / Home Assistant, the HTTP API and firmware updates over Wi-Fi. Off: Bluetooth and USB only, and 3.3 MB instead of 1.9 MB for animations.
options.upload_note: Switching to a build with another partition layout (Wi-Fi, no Wi-Fi, no Wi-Fi with Bluetooth updates; the Flash layout card shows it) erases the animations stored on the buddy: push them again afterwards.

options.label: Bluetooth
options.help: Bluetooth LE control: the phone app, the menu bar app and the Claude Code bridge over Bluetooth (pairing code on the screen).

options.label: Updates over Bluetooth
options.help: New firmware can be sent over Bluetooth from a paired computer ("Update over Bluetooth" below; a few minutes, Bluetooth moves 3 to 5 KB/s). Without Wi-Fi this needs a second app slot, so 2.69 MB instead of 3.31 MB is left for animations.

options.label: USB serial only
options.help: Neither Wi-Fi nor Bluetooth: the buddy is controlled, updated and given animations over its USB cable only (sim/test/push_all.sh usb). The smallest firmware (about 300 KB), with 3.3 MB for animations.

options.label: Battery level
options.help: Measures a LiPo through a divider on GPIO 1, shows the level in every app and plays the battery and charging animations. Off: for buddies that always run on USB power (about 11 KB less firmware).

options.label: Charging status
options.help: Two wires (through small Schottky diodes) from the charger's CHRG and STDBY pads to GPIO 2 and 4: the buddy knows when it is charging and when it is full, and plays the charging animations. Off: leave those wires out.

warnings.text: USB serial only: control, animations and firmware updates go over the USB cable.

env_rules.why: no Wi-Fi + Bluetooth updates: two app slots
